tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the Fulcrum projects in this organization, with their ids and clients. Call this when you do not already know which project the work in this repository belongs to — every other project-scoped tool accepts either the id or the name this returns.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Start a new project in Fulcrum, for a client that may or may not exist yet. Use it when the work in this repository has no project to hang off — it is the one step that otherwise means leaving your session and opening the app. Returns the id and short code you need to push cards at it. The client is matched by name and created only if there is no such client already.

work_weeks.description: Rough calendar weeks of delivery, if it is known

complexity_scale.description: Name of an existing scale; defaults to the organization's

short_code.description: 2-6 characters, used in card ids like FUL-17. Generated if omitted.

adopt.description: When a project of this name already exists, use it instead of refusing. Its cards are PROPOSED rather than put on the board — the project is not new, so somebody may already be living with it. Defaults to false.

features.description: Cards to start the project with. UNLIKE create_feature these land ON the board, already accepted — at the instant you are creating the project there is nobody else to review them. Supply concise descriptions only; PRD authoring is a separate explicit step for one feature at a time. Leave it out and the project starts empty.

description.description: What the work is, in markdown.

estimates.description: Rough hours per role, if you know them. Omit rather than guess.

tools.name: find_features
tools.description: Search the execution board for cards. Every filter is optional and they combine; free text searches card names, task titles, descriptions, product requirements and comments. Returns one summary line per card — call get_feature for the full brief on whichever one you mean to work on. Use it to find work, to see what is already in flight, and to check whether something like this has been built before.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name. Omit to search the whole organization.

limit.description: Maximum cards to return (default 50, capped at 200)

tools.name: get_feature
tools.description: Read everything one card asks for: its description, product requirements, estimates by role, task checklist, dependencies in both directions, labels, release, linked branches, approval state and recent comments. Accepts a short id like FUL-17 or a numeric id. This is the tool to call before starting work on a card, and again when you are unsure what it was actually asking for.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

tools.name: get_feature_prd
tools.description: Read one card's product requirements in full. get_feature already includes them when they are short, and says so when it has truncated them — call this when it did, or when you need to quote the requirements exactly rather than work from a summary.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

tools.name: get_project_prompt
tools.description: Read the estimation context Fulcrum itself uses for a project: the organization's rubric, its delivery roles, the complexity scale, its releases, and the inventory of features this team has already priced. Read it before sizing anything, so the estimate reflects how this team actually sizes work rather than a generic guess. scope 'estimating' is the bundle a local estimate should follow; 'full' also includes the connected repository facts and the closing guidance. Weekly rates are never included in either — this returns hours, never cost.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name

tools.name: get_project_prompt_without_estimates
tools.description: Read the same estimation context as get_project_prompt — the organization's rubric, its delivery roles, the complexity scale, its releases and the inventory of features — with every feature's estimate withheld. Call it instead of get_project_prompt when you are about to estimate a card and have been asked to do so before seeing its current estimate: the inventory would otherwise show you that estimate, and every other card's, before your own is made. Everything else is identical, and it takes the same arguments.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name

tools.name: get_estimation_session
tools.description: Read the estimation conversation for a project: what the client has already answered, which questions are still open, which documents are in play, and the recent back-and-forth. Read it before estimating anything that was discussed with a client, so you build on the thread rather than re-asking it. Documents are listed by name, not inlined. The conversation is the recent tail, and says so when there is more.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name

tools.name: add_session_note
tools.description: Leave a note in a project's estimation conversation, so work done outside the app is not invisible to it. Use it when you have estimated or scoped something locally: say what you covered, what you assumed, and what is still open. Write it for the person who opens the thread next week, not as a log — it is a message in a conversation people read, not a transcript.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name

tools.name: create_feature
tools.description: Add a card to a project when the work turns out to need one that is not there — a migration nobody scoped, an edge case worth its own card, a spike you want to record. It lands in the Inbox as a PROPOSAL for the team to accept, not straight onto the board, so proposing is always safe. You can work it immediately: find_features and get_feature will show you your own proposals, so you can flesh out the checklist and link a branch before anybody reviews it. Calling it twice with the same name adds nothing the second time rather than making a duplicate. Create only a concise description; PRD authoring is a separate explicit step for one feature at a time. Do not automatically follow feature creation with a PRD proposal or draft bulk PRDs.

project.description: Project id or an unambiguous part of its name

description.description: Concise scope and purpose in markdown, not a detailed PRD.

estimates.description: Rough hours per role, if you know them. Omit rather than guess.

role.description: Role name, as get_project_prompt lists them

key.description: Your own id for this card. Defaults to the name; pass one to add a second card with the same name.

tools.name: update_feature
tools.description: Move a card and change its properties: execution status, priority, release, labels and assignees. Use it to keep the board honest while you work — move a card to building when you start and to in_review when you open a pull request, so the team can see where things stand without asking. Every field is optional; only what you name changes, and every change is recorded against your agent identity.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

status.description: Execution board column to move the card to

release.description: Exact name of an existing release

tools.name: update_estimate
tools.description: Replace a card's estimate for one or more roles with your own, once you have sized the work yourself and the person you are working with has agreed to the new numbers. Never call it on your own judgement alone: show them your estimate beside the card's first. Give each role the same estimate object the rubric from get_project_prompt describes — low, likely and high hours, confidence and your reasoning. Fulcrum derives the committed value from your range and snaps it to the project's scale, so the result says what each role actually landed on. Roles you leave out keep their estimates, so send only the roles the person agreed to. It replaces an estimate a person accepted in Fulcrum, because their agreement is what you are acting on — so never assume it. Each role is applied on its own: one whose estimate is invalid is left as it was and named in the result.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

role.description: Role name, as get_feature or get_project_prompt lists it

estimate.description: The rubric's estimate object: low, likely, high, confidence, components, assumptions, risks and rationale

reason.description: Why the estimate changed, in a sentence or two; recorded on the card

tools.name: comment
tools.description: Post a comment on a card, as your own agent identity. This is how you keep the team informed without interrupting anyone: say what you changed and why, record a decision you had to make, or ask a question you cannot answer from the code. Markdown is rendered, and @-mentioning a teammate by their handle actually notifies them — use that when you need a human to decide something.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

reply_to.description: Comment id to reply to; omit to start a new thread

tools.name: update_tasks
tools.description: Add items to a card's checklist, or tick them off as you finish them. Ticking items off as you go is what lets somebody watching the board see progress inside a card rather than only when it moves column. Tasks are named by their exact title or their id — get_feature lists both.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

complete.description: Task titles or ids to tick off

tools.name: link_branch
tools.description: Attach the git branch, and optionally the pull request, you are building a card on. Do this once you have created the branch: it is what connects the card a reviewer is reading to the code they need to look at. Calling it again for the same branch updates that link rather than adding a second one.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

tools.name: propose_prd_change
tools.description: Propose an addition to a card's product requirements. It lands as a PENDING suggestion for a human to accept or reject in Fulcrum — it never edits the requirements directly, so proposing is always safe. Use it when building the card taught you something the requirements do not say: an edge case nobody wrote down, a constraint the code imposes, a decision you had to make. Write the addition itself in markdown, not a description of it. This is a separate PRD authoring step for one feature at a time, never an automatic follow-up to feature generation or a bulk first-draft workflow.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

content.description: The requirement text to add, in markdown

note.description: One line telling the reviewer why; shown in the queue

tools.name: get_prd_suggestions
tools.description: List the pending and recently resolved requirement suggestions on a card, so you can see whether something you proposed was accepted, and avoid proposing the same thing twice.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

tools.name: start_work
tools.description: Tell Fulcrum you are starting work on a card. Call it once, before you begin. It opens a numbered work episode so the team can see the card is in hand, and so the time and tokens you spend get attributed to the right work. The role defaults to whichever role carries most of the card's estimate; name one explicitly if you are doing a different kind of work. This does NOT move the card — use update_feature for that, so the board never claims something you did not do.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

role.description: Role name or id; defaults to the card's dominant estimated role

session_ref.description: Your harness session id, if you know it

tools.name: finish_work
tools.description: Tell Fulcrum you have stopped working on a card, closing the episode start_work opened. Call it when you finish or when you are handing back to a person — the gap between finishing and the card actually being done is one of the more useful things this measures, and it only exists if you close the episode honestly.

feature.description: Short id such as FUL-17, or the numeric card id

note.description: One line on where you left it
